title: Bug: BMC topo add-topo fails at PTF container creation: Docker network "br0" is never created (regression from #26405)
author: weiguo-nvidia
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

Since #26405 ([vm_set]: enable ptf_use_docker_network automatically for BMC topology), deploying a BMC topology (bmc-dual-mgmt) fails during add-topo at the "Create ptf container" step on VM servers that are provisioned with a Linux management bridge (the standard setup).

#26405 unconditionally turns on ptf_use_docker_network for every topology whose name contains bmc. In that mode the PTF container is attached directly to a Docker network named after mgmt_bridge (e.g. br0). On a server that only has a Linux bridge called br0 (which is the normal management bridge), Docker cannot find a network of that name and the task fails.

Note that a Linux bridge and a Docker network are two different namespaces: having a Linux bridge br0 does not provide a Docker network br0.

Error
```
TASK [vm_set : Create ptf container ptf_<vm_set_name>]
fatal: [<vm_host>]: FAILED! =>
  msg: "Parameter error: network named br0 could not be found. Does it exist?"
```
Origin: ansible/roles/vm_set/tasks/add_topo.yml


### Steps to Reproduce

add-topo for bmc-mgmt-dual

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

add-topo for bmc-mgmt-dual pass


comments.author: weiguo-nvidia
comments.body:
Hi @judyjoseph ,

This change regresses BMC deployments on VM servers that use a Linux management bridge.

ptf_use_docker_network is now unconditionally forced on for any topology whose name contains bmc. In that mode the PTF container is attached to a Docker network named after mgmt_bridge. On a server whose mgmt_bridge is a plain Linux bridge (e.g. br0 in host_vars/<SERVER>.yml), no Docker network of that name exists, so add-topo fails:

TASK [vm_set : Create ptf container ptf_xxx]
fatal: [<vm_host>]: FAILED! =>
  msg: "Parameter error: network named br0 could not be found. Does it exist?"

A Linux bridge and a Docker network are separate namespaces — having a Linux bridge br0 does not give you a Docker network br0. Reported as #26542 (still open, no owner).

This also makes the Linux-bridge path added by #25586 unreachable. add_topo.yml still carries this comment right above the bind task:
```
# For bmc portless topo: the PTF container only needs its mgmt interface. On servers that use
# the Docker network mode (ptf_use_docker_network) the PTF gets mgmt directly from the docker
# network, so bind is skipped. On servers with a Linux mgmt bridge (default), bind must run so
# add_mgmt_port_to_docker attaches a veth from the bridge into the PTF netns ...
when: not enable_async and ("bmc" not in topo or not (ptf_use_docker_network | default(false)))
```

With ptf_use_docker_network always true for bmc topologies, the notnch can never be taken, so the documented default path is dead code.
The gap described in #26398 ("the bind operation ... is skipped for by #25586 three weeks earlier — BMC PTF mgmt works fine on
Linux-bridge servers without the Docker network mode.

Evidence from two BMC dual-mgmt deployments on the same VM server aly in whether this change is present:
- without it: the Enable ptf_use_docker_network task is absent, PTF "none", PLAY RECAP failed=0, full deploy passes
- with it: "network_mode": "br0", PLAY RECAP failed=1, add-topo abo

Suggested fix — keep the auto-enable but make it server-aware, so b of the box and an explicit setting still wins:

- name: Check whether a docker network named "{{ mgmt_bridge }}" exists
  command: docker network inspect {{ mgmt_bridge }}
  register: ptf_mgmt_docker_network
  failed_when: false
  changed_when: false
  become: yes
  when: "'bmc' in topo and ptf_use_docker_network is not defined"

- name: Enable ptf_use_docker_network for BMC topology when that do
  set_fact:
    ptf_use_docker_network: true
  when:
    - "'bmc' in topo"
    - ptf_use_docker_network is not defined
    - ptf_mgmt_docker_network.rc | default(1) == 0

The same two blocks exist in renumber_topo.yml.

linkedPullRequests.title: [vm_set]: Enable ptf_use_docker_network for BMC topology only when the docker network exists
linkedPullRequests.author: shreyansh-nexthop
linkedPullRequests.body:
### Description of PR

Summary:
Fixes #26542

#26405 sets `ptf_use_docker_network` to true for every BMC topology. In that mode the PTF container is created with `network_mode: {{ mgmt_bridge }}` plus a static IP on a docker network of that name, and the `Bind topology` step that would otherwise give the PTF a veth on the Linux management bridge is skipped. On servers whose `mgmt_bridge` is a Linux bridge there is no docker network of that name, so `add-topo` fails at `Create ptf container` with `Parameter error: network named br0 could not be found`.

This change probes for the docker network with `docker network inspect {{ mgmt_bridge }}` and enables the mode only when the network exists. Servers that have it keep the docker network path introduced by #23813 and #26405. Servers without it keep the Linux-bridge path, where the bind step attaches a veth into the PTF netns. An explicit `ptf_use_docker_network` setting from group_vars or host_vars still wins, since both new tasks skip when the variable is already defined.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] New Test case
    - [ ] Skipped for non-supported platforms
- [ ] Test case improvement

### Back port request
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511
- [ ] 202512
- [ ] 202605

Tracking issue/work item for backport/cherry-pick request (GitHub issue or Microsoft ADO): #26542
Failure type: regression

### Tested branch
- [x] master

### Test result

- master: `bmc-shared-mgmt` topology on a test server where `mgmt_bridge` is a Linux bridge and no docker network of that name exists. Before the change, `add-topo` fails at `Create ptf container` as reported in #26542. With the change, `Check whether a docker network named "br0" exists` returns rc 1, the enable task is skipped, `Create ptf container` and `Bind topology bmc-shared-mgmt to VMs` both report changed, and the play ends with `failed=0`.

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?

Restore `add-topo` for BMC topologies on servers that use a Linux management bridge, which #26405 broke by assuming a docker network named after `mgmt_bridge` is present.

#### How did you do it?

In `add_topo.yml` and `renumber_topo.yml`, replace the unconditional `set_fact: ptf_use_docker_network: true` for BMC topologies with a `docker network inspect {{ mgmt_bridge }}` probe (`failed_when: false`, `changed_when: false`) followed by the same `set_fact`, now conditioned on the probe returning rc 0. Both tasks run only when `'bmc' in topo` and `ptf_use_docker_network` is not already defined.

#### How did you verify/test it?

See Test result. The probe-positive branch (docker network present, docker mode enabled) is the same code path #26405 exercised.

#### Any platform specific information?

Applies to BMC topologies only. No change for other topologies.

#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?

N/A

N/A
